trusted_external_entities.name: Client Application
trusted_external_entities.description: DApp or web application registering event listeners with the provider
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Client applications are web-based DApps that could be malicious or compromised. They can register arbitrary event listeners and may attempt to abuse the provider API. The provider should validate all interactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Extension
trusted_external_entities.description: Browser extension or application that injects the Ethereum provider
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Wallet extensions are typically vetted through browser extension stores and explicitly installed by users. However, the user must trust the wallet implementation. From the client app's perspective, the wallet has full control over data and could be malicious.

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract
trusted_external_entities.description: Smart contract invoking the ALT_BN128 precompile via CALL/STATICCALL
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Calling contract is EVM-validated bytecode. However, it can provide arbitrary input data to the precompile, so all inputs must be validated. Invalid curve points, field elements >= modulus, and malformed lengths must be rejected.

trusted_external_entities.name: SCO File System
trusted_external_entities.description: Designated directories containing State Change Object files
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: SCO files from the filesystem are external data sources that could be tampered with or maliciously crafted. Files must be verified through security checks (script audit, hardcoded block height, no wallet operations) before trust is established.

security_assumptions: Event names are validated against allowed event types
Listener function cannot directly access provider internals
Duplicate listener handling is implementation-defined but safe
Removing non-existent listener is a no-op
Client can only remove its own registered listeners
Callback count decrement is atomic
User has explicitly installed and trusts the wallet extension
Browser extension isolation prevents unauthorized provider injection
Provider object is the legitimate wallet interface

boundary_edges.edge_label: Caller provides input bytes via message data
data_crossing_boundary: Raw input bytes for curve operations
security_assumptions: Input length validation prevents buffer overflows
Field element validation ensures values < modulus
Point-on-curve validation prevents invalid curve attacks
Invalid input triggers OutOfGasError, consuming all gas
Input length is validated as multiple of 192 bytes
Subgroup order validation prevents invalid curve attacks
Gas cost (34000*n+45000) prevents DoS from large inputs

boundary_edges.edge_label: Client loads SCO files from designated directories at startup
security_assumptions: SCO files are verified through governance process before deployment
Filesystem has not been tampered with by attacker
All network nodes load identical SCO files for consensus

boundary_edges.edge_label: Load SCO file from external filesystem
security_assumptions: Script auditing identifies unsafe operations
Block height must be hardcoded for reproducibility
No unlocked wallets used during verification
Failed security checks prevent SCO execution
